content.summary: Welcome to the reading module on professions, workplaces, and daily job responsibilities. In this lesson, you will read about different workers, learn how to describe what they do, and practice finding key details in short texts.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Present Simple tense for daily routines and job responsibilities using affirmative sentences and questions.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Key profession nouns, workplace locations, and common action verbs related to work.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts to locate specific profession names, workplace locations, and daily job duties.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about different professions and workplaces.
Locate specific details such as job duties, tools, and workplace locations.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns for describing what people do every day.

rules: Use 'What does a/an + profession + do?' to ask about job responsibilities.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Professions, Workplaces & Job Responsibilities

content.summary: Learn how to write clear sentences about jobs, workplace locations, and daily job duties using simple present tense and correct prepositions.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the indefinite article 'a' before consonant sounds and 'an' before vowel sounds for professions.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He is a architect who works in a office.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He is an architect who works in an office.
mechanicsRules.why: Architect and office start with vowel sounds, so they require 'an' instead of 'a'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Add 's' or 'es' to the base verb when describing third-person singular job responsibilities.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: A journalist writes news articles every day.
mechanicsRules.badExample: A journalist write news articles every day.
mechanicsRules.why: Singular profession subjects require the third-person singular present simple verb form.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the preposition 'in' for enclosed indoor spaces and 'at' for specific outdoor or work sites.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Nurses work in hospitals and electricians work at construction sites.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Nurses work at hospitals and electricians work in construction sites.
mechanicsRules.why: Hospitals are enclosed buildings requiring 'in', while construction sites are specific locations requiring 'at'.

pillars.name: Sentence Rhythm
